title: 5 things to know BEFORE you see Avenue Q ⭐️ ⭐️ ⭐️ ⭐️ ⭐️ (London review)
transcript: After 16 years, this much-acclaimed musical is back in London. Avenue Q is one of the crowd favorites, and I went to see it during the first week of previews in London, and I'm here to tell you five things that you need to know before you check out this musical. If you're seeing me for the first time, then hello, I'm Kristina. I share my reviews and creative life in London on my channel, and if you like the sound of it, then make sure to subscribe. I'm also running 2026 theater challenge, and there's 100 of us who have already signed up for it. And if you're interested to check that out, then click on the link description box. Avenue Q is famous for blending the Sesame Street style puppets and adult themes, and all of this makes it a very relatable and highly engaging watch. This has caused that this musical has such a strong fan base since 2003 when it first opened in New York. Famously in 2004 during the Tony Awards ceremony, it took away best musical, best score, and best book away from Wicked, which was the musical that year that was the strongest contender for winning these awards. So, if this doesn't say enough about the acclaim of this musical and how much the world of theater really appreciates it, then I don't know what does. Robert Lopez is the person who wrote this musical, and he's the youngest EGOT winner, which means that he has Emmy, Grammy, Oscar, and Tony Award, and he doesn't have it only once, but he's won this twice, all of them. So, he is super super talented mind and genius whose work isn't only Avenue Q, that is also The Book of Mormon. He also wrote some songs and co-wrote on Frozen and Coco. So, when you get to see Avenue Q, you actually get to see the best of the best in action. And as mentioned, the story explores adult themes of sexuality, racism, finding your purpose, figuring things out once you finish uni and find yourself in a little bit of a limbo about how to proceed forward and how to actually feel like you are doing right in life. And the best part about this story are quite a few really fun and engaging characters who are delivering the story, and who all in one way or the other are struggling with similar issues that all adults face, making their story something that makes every audience member visible. The story of Avenue Q starts when Princeton arrives to Avenue Q looking for an apartment, and he meets Brian and Kate and a few other misfits who live there. So, while Princeton is looking for a job, Kate is looking for love, Rod is closeted gay, Nicky is just not willing to work or do anything outside of his comfort zone. And all of them in this very dysfunctional way create something that is so relatable to everyone who is living through the adulthood today. The second thing to know before you go see Avenue Q is that this is very much a story that is predominantly geared towards adults rather than kids, despite these really quirky and fun puppets. It discusses things that are more suitable for people with more life experience that can relate and understand the satire of the show. This is something that Robert Lopez is known for. If you've seen The Book of Mormon, you know that there is a lot of underlying humor even when the sentences that the characters are saying are just a little bit outrageous. You need to have that understanding of the wider context in order to appreciate it. So, from that perspective, this show is better suited for going out with friends, your partner, and just generally people who are, I would say, even like 18 and above because I think that these are the people who will appreciate it the most because they have enough of the life experience that is referenced in the show that they can really relate with, such as finishing uni or figuring out what to do after, or not being able to find a boyfriend, or not being sure about your sexuality. All these things and experiences really add up to the beauty of the show, but I think it could be a little bit lost on people who are a bit younger and it's just not really as appropriate for them to go see it. The third of my favorite thing that you need to know about this musical is that the music is so contagious, and I can guarantee you that once you come back from the musical, you will listen to it because there are so many great songs that are again so relatable and fun to listen to, and you just realize how many play of words and different moments in the songs there are. The more you listen to it, the more you like them. Some of my favorite numbers in the show are For Now, which is the last song of the whole musical, which actually summarizes the whole philosophy of the show, and that is that the nature of the life is so fleeting, and everything that is happening, such as relationships or losing jobs, even the governments, they're just for now, and you know, we all move on, and life moves on, so we shouldn't be worrying and stressing out about things too much. Another great song is There's a Fine Line, which is all about relationships, and it actually has a really strong message because Kate Monster decides that she doesn't want to be involved with someone who is just wasting her time and is not serious about relationship with her. There are some other fun numbers, such as Everyone's a Little Bit Racist and If You Were Gay, and these are just a sample of songs. Honestly, every single song on this soundtrack is really worth listening to, and in the show, they are very engaging and upbeat, and just the whole pace of the show is so well measured that it doesn't really allow you to get lost in anyone's story, but it just keeps you on your toes. And this is all held by the fact that we're seeing the puppeteers and we're seeing how many different characters they're actually delivering, and this all adds to the dynamic of the show. And just the whole the package of set design and delivery of the show with the music make it such an impactful show to see and ultimately really really comedic night at the theater. The fourth thing to know before you see the show is that actors and cast are impeccable because they don't need to be just great singers and dance well, but they also need to be great puppeteers and delivering these puppets who are super super cute, and also they have their own stories and their own feelings and and their whole vibe to the show. And what is the most impressive part about the cast is that a lot of them are actually delivering more than one character. So, for example, Noah Harrison, who is playing Princeton, he's also playing Rod, Emily Benjamin, who's playing Kate Monster, she's also delivering Lucy the Then Charlie McCollum is delivering Nicky, Trekkie Monster, and Bad Idea Bear. Meg Hupp Lee is delivering Mrs. T and Bad Idea. So, like all of these cast members are delivering more than one character, and it is so nice being able to actually see how they do it on stage because somehow you forget that they're there, but also obviously because of the way they speak and their facial expressions and the way that they carry themselves to help the puppets deliver what they need to deliver. It's just so so so impressive, and I think that this kind of cast actually requires even more of that skill and presence that it is absolutely mind-blowing seeing them deliver it this together. I was particularly impressed by Emily Benjamin and Noah Harrison, who are delivering Kate and Princeton. They're on the stage for a majority of the time. They have great chemistry between the two of them and the puppets. It's just such an interesting thing to see how much you get attached and how much you feel for these characters that are just puppets, and this is all because it's so well delivered by people who are in the show. The fifth thing to know is that set design is very innovative, but is also very static, which is really interesting because obviously they were trying to portray this Avenue Q and different apartments and entering and exiting from them, but there are so many really innovative ways that they have delivered it in or different puppets that you can see in the windows. At certain times, there is like a whole apartment that opens up, and then you can see Kate Monster's apartment or Rod's apartment. It is kind of set that opens itself up, and then it kind of closes back in, and it just feels a little bit like a Lego house, and I think for this type of production, it really worked well. And also just the whole vibe of the show and the way that they were entering and exiting from different points, it just felt very warm and heartfelt and like these are truly the characters who live in this show. So, this is fun way of making it a bit cartoonish because there were also subtle elements of the show that were delivered as a cartoons. But besides those cartoonish elements, you do have the actual set design and how that all unfolds in front of you makes it really fun to watch and engaging. So, I really love that aspect of the show. So, my final verdict of this show is that it's a must-see. It's one of those shows that is full of humor and good energy and ultimately a positive message about life, and it has that underlying irony and satire, which makes it really quirky on top of all these really silly and cute puppets that you can see in the show. with these impeccable performances and great set design, I think that this revival of Avenue Q is going to be something that the existing fans will love, but then also there will be a lot of new people who get introduced to the show for the first time and who will love it because of how relatable and energetic and engaging it is. So, if you're coming to London, then make sure to check out Avenue Q until August 2026 at Shaftesbury Theatre. It is only 2 hours and 20 minutes with the interval, so it's a perfect show for a night out with your friends. It's going to definitely make you laugh and make you feel better about your life.
